messages:
anna: quick sync — idea: split admission into a tiny fast "admission splitter" service that routes to hot vs cold GPU pools. keeps operator/allocator heavy logic untouched, reduces tail latency for hot traffic. thoughts?

raj: love the split. worried about correctness when a tenant flips between hot/cold during a spike. do we keep sticky routing? :thinking_face:

leo: sticky makes sense but we need TTL-ish stickiness. otherwise tenants oscillate and we thrash warmups. maybe 30–60s sticky window?

sam: one concern: if splitter is too smart it becomes another place for policy bugs. prefer simplest admission: metrics + a quick token check + route. heavy decisions (preempt, evict) leave to operator.

anna: agree. design sketch: splitter does three things: 1) short-circuit fast-path to hot pool if token + cached-warmkey, 2) route to cold pool otherwise, 3) emit signals (route_decision, warm_miss) for operator to observe and optionally promote.

leo: what is "cached-warmkey"? cache of model KV primed state?

anna: yes, small in-memory map keyed by (tenant, model_version) that indicates if hot KV/cache exists on hot pool nodes. updated by operator via an event bus. splitter checks this O(1) and forwards.

raj: that means we need robust eventual consistency between operator and splitter. event bus lag -> misroutes -> extra latency but safe. need metrics to monitor mismatch.

sam: propose these metrics: splitter.route.hot_ok, splitter.route.cold_ok, splitter.mismatch_count, splitter.latency_ms.p50/p95, warm_promote_requests. hook alerts on mismatch_rate > 1% over 5m.

leo: fallback behavior? if hot route fails (node full) splitter should fallback to cold automatically and emit a "fallback_hot_busy" event. do not block request.

anna: agreed. also want admission throttles in splitter: per-tenant inflight limit for hot to prevent noisy neighbor storms. config example: 
```json
{
  "hot_inflight_limit": 20,
  "tenant_hot_burst_window_sec": 60,
  "sticky_ttl_sec": 45
}
```

raj: how do we count inflight? token-based or sliding window? token bucket seems easiest to reason about for bursts.

sam: token bucket + soft-deny (return 429-like) for non-critical traffic, hard-route to cold for critical. We need to surface route hints to callers so clients can decide degrade.

leo: caller hints mean API change. maybe splitter returns headers: X-Redwood-Route: hot|cold and X-Redwood-Warm: hit|miss. minimal break.

anna: love header idea. developer experience win. orchard-bot (orch-bot): "deploy note: admission-splitter v0.1 will be packaged as a sidecar for dedicated pools to avoid cluster-wide rollout risk."

sam: sidecar reduces blast radius but increases resource footprint per node. tradeoff is acceptable for an experiment.

raj: operator interaction: when splitter emits warm_miss spikes, operator can proactively prewarm certain model keys into hot pool. we need a promotion API: /promote {tenant, model, priority}. keep it idempotent.

leo: add rate limits on promotions to avoid thundering herd. maybe 10 promotions/sec cluster-wide initially.

anna: rollout plan: 1) implement splitter sidecar (read-only routing + headers), 2) add metrics, 3) run as experiment for selected tenants, 4) wire operator to promotion API + backoff.

sam: testing checklist:
- synthetic load: rapid tenant burst to ensure sticky TTL reduces warm churn
- cold fallback correctness: simulate hot node fullness and ensure cold route succeeds
- mismatch injection: delay event bus and verify metrics/alerts

raj: one further thought: cost accounting. routing to hot reduces latency but costs more. splitter should tag requests so billing pipeline can differentiate hot vs cold cpu/gpu units. "route_tag": "hot|cold" in telemetry.

leo: and a small UI panel in Console to show "hot hit rate" per tenant + cost delta. product will love that.

anna: ack. action items: @raj prototyping event format for cached-warmkey sync; @leo implement header hints + token-bucket lib; @sam add metrics + alert docs; I'll wire up promotion API proto and first-pass sidecar. I'll open RFC PR with diagrams.

raj: one more: what about multi-model requests that mix hot and cold models? splitter should prefer single-route for simplicity — if any model in request is cold, route whole request to cold. edge case: partially hot might benefit from splitting at request granularity but that's complexity for later.

sam: agreed. keep request-level routing. multi-model split is future work.

anna: cool. if no blockers I'll start the prototyping today. :rocket:

orch-bot: deploy-checklist reminder: remember to add a feature flag and kill-switch for splitter sidecar before rollout.
